items.title: Pay "Aktualisierungsgebühr" for vehicle registration data
items.computation: The letter prints an explicit calendar date for payment: 30.11.2026 (a Monday, not a weekend or public holiday in NW), so no adjustment under §193 BGB is needed. The date is simply used as written.

warnings: This letter shows strong signs of being a scam/phishing attempt: there is no real German authority called "Zentralregister Fahrzeugdaten Deutschland" responsible for vehicle holder data (that is handled by the local Kfz-Zulassungsstelle / KBA, not a private "Postfach" entity in Berlin).

The payment IBAN (LT98 7044 0001 1820 4477) is a Lithuanian account, and the named recipient "R. Kazlauskas" is an individual person, not an official German authority account — a legitimate German authority would never request payment to a foreign personal bank account.

The letter uses pressure tactics (claiming the vehicle registration/Zulassung could 'ruhen' from January 2027 and threatening to report the matter to the Zulassungsstelle) to push a quick, unverified payment — a classic fake-registry/fake-fee scam pattern similar to fraudulent 'Gewerbeauskunft'-style letters.

No Rechtsbehelfsbelehrung (legal remedy instructions) is present, which is unusual for a genuine administrative fee notice but consistent with a scam letter designed to look official without being a real administrative act.

Recommendation: do not pay this invoice; verify any supposed vehicle data update requirement directly with your local Zulassungsstelle (KFZ registration office), and consider reporting this letter to the police as a suspected scam.
